newsitem.title: USA: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.
newsitem.headline: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.

text.p: Boxed beef traded sharply higher early in the trading period on light to moderate demand and offerings, USDA said. At the start, processors forced boxed prices sharply higher on very light slaughter numbers, trying to attain a more equable return.
Processors continued to struggle with rather large losses most of the week, demand continued fairly light for all retail, export and HRI needs for the balance of the week.
Rib, chuck and round cut prices were sharply higher early, but as the week progressed some of these early gains were lost as slaughter numbers increased by midweek.

Loin cuts also showed gains, mainly the tenderloins cuts and cuts from the lighter weight carcass. Thin meat and credit items showed higher price levels all week. These particular items were stimulated by demand for value-added product.

Closely trimmed product items also traded at higher price levels on rather light retail demand for the week. Beef trimmings traded sharply higher on moderate demand and light offerings. Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items were higher on fairly good demand mostly in retail areas, as many retailers were wanting to feature ground beef for their immediate needs.

For the week - Select and Choice rib primal 4.00 to 6.00 higher; Select and Choice chuck primal 4.50 to 7.00 higher; Select and Choice round primal 5.00 to 6.00 higher; Select and Choice loin primal 3.00 to 4.00 higher; Closely trimmed items 4.00 to 6.00 higher; Beef trimmings 5.00 higher; Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items 3.00 to 5.00 higher.

The Estimated Composite of Boxed Beef Cutout values of Choice 1-3 550/700 carcasses Up 4.56 at 110.80; 700/850 Up 4.91 at 109.74; Select 1-3 550/700 carcasses Up 5.59 at 104.76; 700/850 Up 4.62 at 103.34.

COW AND BULL CARCASS, BONELESS PROCESSING BEEF, CUTTER COW CUTOUT The boneless beef market continued to move higher this week. Light, early-week slaughter numbers resulted in light offerings which helped to push price levels higher. Grinders grudgingly accepted a modest increase in asking prices but reduced their overall demand which halted further price advances. Cow carcasses moved higher in reaction to the across-the-board price increase in grinding materials.
Cow cuts traded at generally steady levels on reduced demand, especially for 100% lean items where many processors dipped into their freezer stocks to cover much of their needs.

Utility carcasses 2.00 higher; Cutter 1.50-2.00 higher; Fresh 90% boneless beef 3.00-3.50 higher; 85% 2.00-4.00 higher; 75% 1.00-3.00 higher; 65% 5.00-6.00 higher. The Cutter cow carcass gross cut-out value for Thursday, October 03, 1996 was estimated at 67.32 per cwt, up 1.87 from Friday.
